mainTopic: Whether a ספק can override a ודאי, and רבי יוחנן's challenges to ריש לקיש's ruling that an idol that broke by itself is permitted.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: a נפל was thrown into a pit in רימון, a כהן peered in, and the חכמים ruled him טהור because martens and polecats may have dragged it away. The גמרא asks whether this means a ספק can override a ודאי. It gives two answers. First, maybe it was only something that looked like a נפל, and the כהן first checked whether it was a real baby at all. Second, since those animals are common there, they surely dragged it away. The גמרא then returns to the argument about an idol that broke by itself, which ריש לקיש permits. רבי יוחנן raises a series of challenges from sources that forbid an idol a ישראל damaged. אביי and רבא answer, and רבא explains that such cases are forbidden only by a rabbinic decree, in case the ישראל lifts the idol and makes it his own. That answer is reused for the stones of מרקוליס, the shaved idol, the ground-up idol and the beheaded dragon. Finally, the leaves of a worshipped tree stay forbidden because the tree, the main idol, is still whole.

steps.title: The stillborn in the pit at רימון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells of a maidservant who threw a נפל into a pit. A כהן looked in, and the חכמים ruled him טהור because animals there may have dragged it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...of a certain oppressor in רימון, who threw a stillborn baby into a pit. A כהן came and peered in to find out whether it was male or female. The case came before the חכמים and they declared him טהור, because weasels and martens are common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of a ברייתא. It is bringing this case as a source to test whether a doubt can override something certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead body in the pit would make the כהן who leaned over it טמא. The חכמים still ruled him טהור, because animals in that area may have carried the body away before he looked. Their reason depends only on that doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: And they declared him ritually pure
A polecat or similar wild animal

phrases.english: of a certain oppressor in Rimon,
phrases.notes: We're joining the ברייתא mid-sentence. It began with 'an incident with the maidservant' of this man.

phrases.english: who cast a stillborn into a pit,
and a priest came and peered in
to know whether it was male or female,
and the incident came before the Sages
and they declared him pure,
because weasels and martens are common there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a ספק can override a ודאי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the maidservant in רימון, where the כהן was ruled טהור because of a doubt

steps.title: Here a doubt overrides a certainty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out its point: the נפל was certainly thrown in and it is only a doubt whether it was dragged away, yet the doubt wins.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, it is certain that she threw in a stillborn, and it is only a doubt whether animals dragged it away or not. Yet the doubt comes and overrides the certainty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the challenge out of the ברייתא. It shows that this case seems to let a doubt beat a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The certain fact is that a body was put in the pit. The only doubt is whether it was removed. Ruling the כהן טהור means the doubt overrode the certainty, which goes against the idea that a ספק cannot override a ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes something out of its certain status

phrases.english: But here,
where she certainly cast a stillborn,
it is uncertain whether they dragged it away,
uncertain whether they did not drag it away,
and a doubt comes and takes it out of the certainty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 1 to make the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that a ספק cannot override a ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has a certain impurity (a body in the pit) and only a doubt that it was removed, yet the ruling follows the doubt.

steps.title: Maybe it only looked like a stillborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא should be read as 'something like a נפל,' so the presence of a body was never certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say she threw a stillborn into the pit. Say instead: she threw something that looked like a stillborn into the pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rereading the ברייתא. It wasn't certain the object was a real נפל at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the object might not have been a body, there was never a certain impurity. The case becomes a doubt against a doubt (was it a body, and was it dragged away), not a doubt against a certainty. So the principle stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say... rather, say (a way of rereading a text)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the חכמים allowed a doubt to beat a certainty. It is saying the certainty was never there in the first place.

phrases.english: Do not say she cast a stillborn into a pit,
rather, say:
she cast something like a stillborn into a pit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא הֵטִילָה נֵפֶל לְבוֹר אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source text (לא תימא... אלא אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא describes a definite נפל, so a doubt overrode a certainty.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was only something that looked like a נפל, so it is a doubt against a doubt.

steps.title: But the כהן checked if it was male or female
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The ברייתא says the כהן wanted to know the baby's sex, which shows it was surely a real נפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says he looked 'to know whether it was male or female'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 3, using the ברייתא's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody asks whether a lump of blood is male or female. Asking about the sex shows the only open question was the sex, and that it really was a נפל. That brings back the certainty the answer tried to remove.

phrases.english: But isn't it: 'to know whether it was male'
'or female' that is taught!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לֵידַע אִם זָכָר אִם נְקֵבָה הוּא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3 using the wording of the ברייתא from step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Checking whether it was male or female only makes sense if it was surely a real נפל. So the certainty is back.

steps.title: The כהן first checked whether it was even a baby
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the כהן had two questions: was it a shapeless mass or a real נפל, and only if it was a נפל, was it male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: he wanted to know if she miscarried a shapeless mass or threw in a נפל. And if you say it was a נפל, he wanted to know if it was male or female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 4 by rereading the ברייתא. The question about male or female came second, after the first question of whether there was a real baby at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 argued that asking about the sex proves a real נפל was surely thrown in. The גמרא answers that the כהן's first question was whether it was a נפל or just a shapeless mass. The sex question only applies if it turns out to be a נפל, so the body's presence was still never certain, and the answer from step 3 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; the גמרא explains how to read a source
Literally 'wind'; here a shapeless mass that is not a real baby
And if you will say; and if it turns out that

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
to know whether she miscarried a shapeless mass,
phrases.notes: רוח literally means 'wind'. Here it means a formless mass, not a real baby, so it does not make anything טמא.

phrases.english: or whether she threw in a נפל,
and if you say that she threw in a נפל,
to know whether it was male or female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 and so protects the answer of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא: the sex question depends on an earlier question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sex question showed a real נפל was surely there.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן first checked whether it was a נפל at all, so there was no certain body.

steps.title: Second answer: the animals surely dragged it away
steps.stepSummary: A different answer: since martens and polecats are common there, it is certain they dragged the body away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: since martens and polecats are common there, they certainly dragged it away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, separate answer to the challenge of step 2. It accepts that there really was a נפל, but says the dragging away was also a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2's challenge was that a mere doubt (maybe it was dragged) beat a certainty (a נפל was there). This answer says the dragging was not a doubt. Since these animals are always around there, they surely dragged it, so it is a certainty against a certainty, and the rule that a doubt cannot override a certainty is not broken.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say; introduces a second, different answer
A polecat, a wild animal that drags things off

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a further step built on step 5. It is a separate answer to the same challenge, so you can pick either one.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the rule that a doubt does not override a certainty (אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי) without needing to reread the ברייתא.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
since martens and polecats are common there,
they certainly dragged it away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 2, instead of the answer of steps 3 and 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the doubt as a certainty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dragging away was only a doubt, which seemed to beat a certainty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dragging is certain because the animals are common there, so it is a certainty against a certainty.

steps.title: Challenge from the found hand and foot shapes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: the משנה forbids found pieces shaped like a hand or foot, even though they look like broken pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: if one found the shape of a hand or the shape of a foot, they are forbidden, because things like them are worshipped. Why? They are broken pieces!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument about an idol that broke by itself. It brings our משנה as a challenge to ריש לקיש, who holds that broken pieces are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that pieces of a broken idol are permitted. The משנה says a found hand or foot shape is forbidden. A hand or foot looks like a piece broken off an idol, so the משנה seems to say broken pieces are forbidden, against ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן challenging ריש לקיש, using our own משנה.

phrases.english: if one found the shape of a hand or the shape of a foot,
these are forbidden,
because things like them are worshipped.
Why? They are broken pieces!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the נפל discussion and returns to the main argument about a broken idol.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that pieces of a broken idol are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hand or foot shape looks like a broken piece, yet the משנה forbids it, so broken pieces should be forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל: they stand on their own bases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל already explained the משנה as talking about hand and foot shapes standing on their own bases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't שמואל already explain it: when they stand on their bases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to שמואל's explanation of the משנה. The hand and foot in the משנה are standing on their own bases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a hand or foot stands on its own base, it was made that way from the start as a complete object of worship. So it is not a broken piece at all, and the משנה says nothing against ריש לקיש's view that real broken pieces are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it; he interpreted the source

steps.whatToRemember: The hand and foot in the משנה are forbidden because they stand on their own bases, so they were made whole that way. They are not broken pieces, so ריש לקיש's view stands.

phrases.english: Didn't שמואל already explain it:
when they are standing on their bases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hand and foot in the משנה are broken pieces of an idol.
steps.terutzMaskana: They stand on their own bases, so they were made whole that way and are not broken pieces.

steps.title: Why can't a Jew nullify a gentile's idol?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a משנה: a גוי can nullify an idol, but a ישראל cannot nullify a גוי's idol. According to ריש לקיש, a Jew's breaking should count like the idol breaking by itself, which would make it permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: A gentile can nullify his own idol or his fellow's, but a Jew cannot nullify a gentile's idol. Why? Let it be like an idol that broke by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against ריש לקיש from a משנה about who can nullify an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that an idol that broke by itself is permitted, even though no גוי nullified it. If so, when a ישראל breaks it, that should be just as good. So why does the משנה say a ישראל cannot nullify a גוי's idol?

keyTerms.meaning: Nullifies; cancels the idol's forbidden status

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is challenging ריש לקיש again.

phrases.english: A gentile can nullify an idol
his own and that of his fellow,
but a Jew cannot nullify
the idol of a gentile.
Why?
Let it be like an idol
that broke by itself!
phrases.notes: No גוי nullified it, yet ריש לקיש permits it. So a Jew breaking it should be no worse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 answered the first challenge, a new challenge is brought against ריש לקיש from a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that an idol that broke by itself is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If breaking without a גוי's nullification is enough, a ישראל breaking a גוי's idol should also work. But the משנה says it does not.

steps.title: The Jew only bent the idol
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה is talking about a ישראל who bent the idol out of shape but did not break it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is talking about where he flattened it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends ריש לקיש by narrowing the משנה to a case where the idol was only bent, not broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idol that is actually broken would be like 'broke by itself,' and ריש לקיש would permit it. But the משנה is about bending, which is not breaking, so the משנה does not contradict ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He flattened it / bent it out of shape

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Where he flattened it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a ישראל who broke the idol, which would contradict ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a ישראל who only bent the idol, so ריש לקיש's ruling about broken idols still stands.

steps.title: Bending does nullify an idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: another משנה says bending an idol nullifies it, even if nothing was removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he flattened it, what of it? But didn't we learn: If he flattened it, even though he did not remove any of it, he nullified it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer with a different משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said bending is not enough to nullify the idol. But a משנה says bending is enough, even without taking anything off. So moving the case to bending does not explain why the ישראל cannot nullify it.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?
But didn't we learn in a משנה?

phrases.english: And if he flattened it, what of it?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: פְּחָסָהּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא חִסְּרָהּ
phrases.english: If he flattened it, even though he did not remove any of it,
he has nullified it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי פְּחָסָהּ מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that bending the idol would not nullify it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that bending nullifies an idol, so the bending case should also be nullified.

steps.title: Bending works only when a gentile does it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the משנה that says bending nullifies is about a גוי bending it. When a ישראל bends it, it is not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies when a gentile flattened it, but if a Jew flattened it, he has not nullified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by explaining that the two משניות are talking about different people doing the bending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bending is a way of nullifying, but only a גוי can nullify. A ישראל's bending is not a nullification, and since the idol is not broken, it is not like 'broke by itself' either. So it stays forbidden, and ריש לקיש is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only to this case)

phrases.english: This applies when a gentile flattened it,
but if a Jew flattened it,
he has not nullified it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 and completes אביי's approach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bending nullifies an idol no matter who does it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a גוי's bending nullifies. A ישראל's bending does not.

steps.title: רבא: a rabbinic decree blocks the Jew's nullification
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently: by the basic law, a ישראל's bending would nullify the idol. But חכמים decreed against it, because the ישראל might pick it up first, and an idol owned by a ישראל can never be nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Actually, when a Jew flattens it, it is also nullified. But it is a decree, lest he lift it up and then nullify it. Then it becomes an idol in a Jew's possession, and any idol in a Jew's possession can never be nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to רבי יוחנן's challenge in step 9, explaining the משנה as a rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said a ישראל's bending does not work at all. רבא says it would work by the basic law, but חכמים forbade it. The fear is that the ישראל will lift the idol, which makes it his, and an idol owned by a ישראל is forbidden forever. Either way, the משנה does not contradict ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree made by חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers protect ריש לקיש. אביי: a ישראל who bends a גוי's idol does not nullify it at all. רבא: by the basic law it is nullified, but חכמים decreed against it, because an idol owned by a ישראל can never be nullified.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא holds that a ישראל's bending does nullify the idol by the basic law. The ban is only a rabbinic decree, made because of what might happen if he lifts it first.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches an important rule: an idol that comes into a ישראל's possession can never be nullified.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Actually, when a Jew flattened it
it is also nullified,
but it is a decree
lest he lift it up
phrases.notes: Lifting an object is a way of taking ownership of it, so now the idol is his.

phrases.english: and then nullify it,
and it becomes an idol in a Jew's possession,
and any idol in a Jew's possession
can never be nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from אביי's approach (steps 10-12) to the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ישראל's bending is not a valid way to nullify an idol at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: By the basic law it works, but חכמים decreed against it, so that a ישראל would not acquire the idol and make it forbidden forever.

steps.title: Stones taken from a מרקוליס pile and used for roads
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא: if a גוי takes stones from a מרקוליס pile and paves roads with them, they are permitted. If a ישראל does it, they are forbidden. According to ריש לקיש, why aren't they permitted, like an idol that broke by itself?
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: A גוי who brought stones from a מרקוליס and paved roads and theaters with them, they are permitted. A ישראל who brought stones from a מרקוליס and paved roads and theaters with them, they are forbidden. Why? Let it be like an idol that broke by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש again, this time with a ברייתא about stones taken from a מרקוליס pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling stones out of the pile damages the idol. ריש לקיש permits an idol that broke by itself, and רבי יוחנן argues that stones a ישראל removed should be no worse. But this ברייתא says that when a ישראל does it, the stones are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Mercury, an idol that was worshipped by throwing stones onto a pile

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not why the ישראל did something wrong. The question is about the stones themselves: according to ריש לקיש, they should have become permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: גּוֹי שֶׁהֵבִיא אֲבָנִים מִן הַמַּרְקוּלִיס,
phrases.english: He objected: A gentile who brought stones from the Mercury pile,
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is challenging ריש לקיש again.

phrases.english: and paved roads and theaters with them — they are permitted,
and a Jew who brought stones from the Mercury pile
and paved roads and theaters with them — they are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי? תֶּיהְוֵי כַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּבְּרָה מֵאֵלֶיהָ!
phrases.english: Why? Let it be like an idol that broke by itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to ריש לקיש, coming after רבא's answer in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that an idol which broke by itself is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids stones a ישראל took from a מרקוליס. ריש לקיש's view would permit them.

steps.title: Answered with רבא's decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this case also fits רבא: the stones are forbidden only because of a rabbinic decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in a few words, by pointing back to רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By basic law, the stones would be permitted, just as ריש לקיש says. חכמים forbade them anyway, in case the ישראל picks up the idol first and makes it his own. A Jew's idol can never be nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: Like רבא, meaning according to his explanation

phrases.english: Here too, it is like Rava.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 13: חכמים decreed against it, in case the ישראל picks up the idol first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses an existing explanation (a rabbinic decree) instead of a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that, by basic law, a Jew's damage does not permit the idol.
steps.terutzMaskana: Basic law would permit the stones. The prohibition is only a decree of חכמים.

steps.title: Shaving pieces off an idol
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings another ברייתא. When a גוי shaves an idol for his own use, the idol and the shavings are permitted. When he shaves it for the idol's sake, the idol is forbidden but the shavings are permitted. When a ישראל shaves it either way, both are forbidden. According to ריש לקיש, why?
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: A גוי who shaved an idol for his own needs: it and its shavings are permitted. For its needs: it is forbidden and its shavings are permitted. A ישראל who shaved an idol, whether for his needs or for its needs: it and its shavings are forbidden. Why? Let it be like an idol that broke by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a second ברייתא against ריש לקיש, this time about shaving pieces off an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a ישראל shaves the idol for his own use, he is damaging it. ריש לקיש would treat that like the idol breaking by itself, which makes it permitted. Yet the ברייתא forbids both the idol and its shavings.

keyTerms.meaning: Its shavings, the pieces scraped off
For its needs, to improve the idol

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the difference between לְצׇרְכּוֹ (for his own needs) and לְצׇרְכָּהּ (for the idol's needs). It is just one letter.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: גּוֹי שֶׁשִּׁיפָּה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לְצׇרְכּוֹ —
phrases.english: He objected: A gentile who shaved an idol for his own needs —
it and its shavings are permitted,
for its needs — it is forbidden, but its shavings are permitted,
and a Jew who shaved an idol,
whether for his own needs or for its needs —
it and its shavings are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי? תֶּיהְוֵי כַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּבְּרָה מֵאֵלֶיהָ!
phrases.english: Why? Let it be like an idol that broke by itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge of the same kind as step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that an idol which broke by itself is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ישראל who shaves an idol for his own use is damaging it. ריש לקיש's view would permit it, but the ברייתא forbids it.

steps.title: Again answered with רבא's decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: the prohibition here is also only רבא's rabbinic decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the shaving challenge exactly as it answered the stones challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By basic law, a Jew's shaving would nullify the idol. The ברייתא forbids it only because חכמים worried the ישראל might pick up the idol first and make it his own. So none of these ברייתות disproves ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullifying an idol so that it becomes permitted
Picked up, which is a way of taking ownership

steps.whatToRemember: Every case where a ישראל's damage leaves an idol forbidden is explained by רבא's decree. The basic law still follows ריש לקיש's approach.

phrases.english: Here too, it is like Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses an existing explanation (a rabbinic decree) instead of a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The shaving ברייתא seemed to show that a Jew's damage does not nullify an idol.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prohibition is only a decree of חכמים. ריש לקיש's view still holds by basic law.

steps.title: The ground-up idol of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a source where even an idol ground into dust stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: רבי יוסי says one grinds up the idol and scatters it to the wind or throws it into the sea. The חכמים said to him: even that becomes fertilizer, and the פסוק says 'nothing of the banned things shall cling to your hand.' So why is it forbidden? Let it be like an idol that broke by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a third source against ריש לקיש. In this source, even the dust of a ground-up idol may not be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says to get rid of the idol by grinding it up and scattering it. The חכמים object that the dust could still help a ישראל, as fertilizer, so it is still forbidden. רבי יוחנן asks: according to ריש לקיש, a smashed idol should be like one that broke by itself, so why is the dust still forbidden?

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is challenging ריש לקיש again, the same way he did in the last few steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
He grinds it and scatters it to the wind
or throws it into the sea.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַף הִיא נַעֲשֵׂית זֶבֶל,
phrases.english: They said to him: it too becomes fertilizer,
and it is written: "Nothing shall cling to your hand
of the banned things."
Why?
Let it be like an idol that broke by itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third objection in the same series as steps 14 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a broken idol is treated like one that broke by itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even ground-up dust stays forbidden, so breaking an idol apart does not seem to make it permitted.

steps.title: Again, it is רבא's decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ground-up idol is forbidden only because of רבא's rabbinic decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it follows רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same short answer it gave before. The prohibition here is only the חכמים's decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the basic law, ריש לקיש's view could still allow the dust. But the חכמים forbade it because a ישראל handled the idol, as רבא explained. So the source does not disprove ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Here too,
it is like Rava.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 13: the חכמים made a decree, even though the basic law would allow it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The prohibition is explained as a rabbinic decree, not the basic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dust is forbidden by the basic law, which would go against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dust is forbidden only by רבא's decree, so ריש לקיש's view still stands.

steps.title: The dragon figure with its head cut off
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from רבי יוסי בן יסיאן: a dragon figure that a ישראל definitely beheaded is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: רבי יוסי בן יסיאן says, if someone found a dragon figure with its head cut off, and it is unsure whether a גוי or a ישראל cut it, it is permitted. If a ישראל definitely cut it, it is forbidden. Why? Let it be like an idol that broke by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a fourth source against ריש לקיש. When a ישראל definitely broke the idol, it stays forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גוי may have cut off the head, the figure is permitted. If a ישראל surely cut it, it is forbidden. רבי יוחנן asks: according to ריש לקיש, a broken idol should be like one that broke by itself, so why is it forbidden when a ישראל broke it?

keyTerms.meaning: A dragon figure, a shape used in idol worship

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
Rabbi Yosei ben Yasian says:
If one found the figure of a dragon
with its head cut off,
uncertain whether a gentile cut it
or whether a Jew cut it, it is permitted,
but if a Jew definitely cut it, it is forbidden.
Why?
Let it be like an idol that broke by itself!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יָסְיָאן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth objection in the same series.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a broken idol is treated like one that broke by itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A figure that a ישראל broke stays forbidden, so his breaking does not seem to permit it.

steps.title: The same answer, from רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers again that the dragon figure is forbidden only because of רבא's rabbinic decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it follows רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dragon case the same way as the earlier cases. This is the last challenge answered with רבא's decree; the next step brings one more challenge that needs a different answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a ישראל definitely cut the figure, it is forbidden only because of the חכמים's decree, not by the basic law. So this source does not disprove ריש לקיש either.

keyTerms.meaning: From the חכמים (rabbinic), not from the basic Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: All four of רבי יוחנן's sources (steps 14, 16, 18, 20) get the same answer. Whenever a ישראל was involved, the prohibition is only רבא's rabbinic decree. So ריש לקיש's view is not disproven.

phrases.english: Here too,
it is like Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The prohibition is explained as a rabbinic decree, not the basic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A figure that a ישראל cut is forbidden by the basic law, which would go against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden only by רבא's decree, so ריש לקיש's view still stands.

steps.title: Challenge from leaves falling off a worshipped tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן cites רבי יוסי: vegetables may not be planted under a worshipped tree in the rainy season, because its falling leaves fertilize them. This suggests that leaves falling on their own stay forbidden, against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: רבי יוסי says you may not even plant vegetables there in the rainy season, because the leaves fall on them. Why should that matter? The fallen leaves should be like an idol that broke on its own, which ריש לקיש permits!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings another source to challenge ריש לקיש. A ברייתא treats leaves that fell off a worshipped tree by themselves as still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says that an idol which broke on its own becomes permitted. Leaves falling off the tree are like pieces breaking off an idol by themselves. So if the leaves are still forbidden, ריש לקיש's rule seems to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The rainy season, when leaves fall
Broke on its own, with no person breaking it

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is challenging ריש לקיש again, like in the last few steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says,
not even vegetables in the rainy season,
phrases.notes: He means you may not plant vegetables under a tree that is worshipped as an idol.

phrases.english: because the foliage falls on them.
Why?
Let it be like an idol
that broke on its own!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge in the series of challenges by רבי יוחנן against ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that an idol which broke on its own is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leaves falling by themselves are like an idol breaking by itself. If רבי יוסי still forbids them, an idol that broke on its own should also stay forbidden.

steps.title: The tree itself is still standing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that falling leaves are different, because the main idol, the tree, still exists whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the main idol still exists.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by showing that the leaves case is not like a broken idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a broken idol, the idol itself is ruined, so it can become permitted. Here the tree, which is the real idol, is still standing and whole. Losing some leaves does not break the idol, so the leaves stay forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's rule applies only when the idol itself is broken. Pieces that fall off an idol which is still whole stay forbidden.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since the main idol still exists.
phrases.notes: The main idol here is the tree itself, which is still standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaves falling off a worshipped tree look the same as an idol breaking on its own.
steps.terutzMaskana: A broken idol is ruined, but a tree that drops leaves remains a whole idol. So its leaves stay forbidden, and ריש לקיש's rule still stands.
